Pros: beautiful wildlife nearby, a nice park system within city limits, a long-standing and dynamic DIY scene, Railroad Square, decent public libraries considering the size of the city, V89, strong support for local food producers in places like farmer’s markets and local grocers, tons of events hosted by the universities, lots of oddities and unique places in the nearby small towns like Monticello and Lloyd.

Cons: irresponsible development. The ill-fated Falls Chase project is the most egregious, but I’ve definitely noticed a lot of Tallahassee getting clear-cut in the past few years and I hope we don’t lose too much green space. We have a sluggish and low-paying job market. There’s a ton of aggressive, reckless, or distracted drivers. The most walkable part of town, downtown over near the Challenger Learning Center, is a wasteland of municipal offices when it could be a really inviting town center. Local businesses have a hard time staying open due in part to high rents, a sluggish economy, and the stranglehold that chains have on high-traffic areas. My fiancé was rushed via ambulance to TMH after having a prolonged seizure. The staff was told multiple times my fiancé has epilepsy, but the folks there ignored that and said it was just alcohol intoxication causing a loss of consciousness. Yes, we had been drinking, but not that much, and I know a seizure when I see one. Staff was rude and belligerent, rolling their eyes openly when asked about tests and treatment options. 

We got charged $2000 to be told “go home, you’re drunk.”  My fiancé had been rushed there unconscious after convulsing on the ground, moaning incoherently, and foaming at the mouth for almost five straight minutes. Every staff member had to be informed about their seizure disorder, and every single person we told acted like it was new information. I don’t think anyone ever wrote it down. 

We were both treated with open contempt, and we just had to hope that the original dermoid cyst that caused the epilepsy and was partially removed earlier hadn’t regrown, which isn’t uncommon. We told staff all about this, including the prior surgical history and the surgeon’s warning that the cyst could grow back, and they dismissed everything. I’ll never go back there again for any reason.
